subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: WEBFRANK NOW HAS A THIRD SANCTIONED MECHANISM: `equivalent_copy_form`, an opcode-CHANGING but value-preserving rewrite of one word to the target's equivalent copy encoding. It is count-preserving (one word in, one word out) so it does not disturb claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-instruction-count-deltas.20260831.v1 or its count-asymmetric sibling; both remain in force and are still the FIRST screen. THE ARCHITECTURAL FACT THE CLASS RESTS ON, and the trap it exists to make unreachable: `mr rD,rS` is `or rD,rS,rS`, which reads GPR rS for ANY rS including r0; `addi rD,rA,0` computes rA+0 but treats a ZERO rA FIELD as the literal value zero, so `addi rD,r0,0` is `li rD,0` and NOT a copy of r0. The two encodings are therefore equivalent exactly when rS != 0, and diverge exactly at rS == 0. decode_copy_form returns ('copy',rD,rS) only for `addi` with a non-zero rA and for `or rD,rS,rS` with Rc CLEAR (`mr.` also writes CR0, which no addi does, so the record-setting form is refused); it returns ('li',rD,K) for the zero-rA addi, and None for everything else. The rS!=r0 check is thus not a separate test that could be forgotten but a structural consequence of the decoder: a target word that copies from r0 decodes as a constant load, fails the 'target must be a copy' precondition, and the rule refuses it. TWO PROOF MODES, named explicitly in each edit so a rule can never silently take the weaker one. `unconditional`: our word and the target word decode as the SAME copy rD<-rS with rS!=0 — pure encoding choice, no dataflow needed. `dominating_def`: our word is `li rD,K`, the target is a copy rD<-rS with rS!=0, and prove_constant_source discharges the value-equivalence obligation by a backward scan that fails closed on the FIRST of: an index reachable by anything but its own fallthrough edge (computed from the existing audited _successors, so any control form whose targets cannot be established already raises), any control instruction in the span (which covers calls clobbering volatiles), any relocated word in the span (a relocated `li` is an address half, not a literal), any write of rS that is not the sought `li rS,K`, and a constant mismatch. Reaching the definition with none of those makes rS equal to K on every path into the site. Additional preconditions on every edit: equal aligned function sizes, no relocation on the rewritten word in EITHER object, matching destination register (a differing destination is a recolor, which is the other stage's job, and is refused here by name), no duplicate offsets, and a per-word assert that the rewrite reaches the target word, on top of apply_patch's unchanged whole-function after_sha256 assert. The stage runs BEFORE the recolor snapshot, so verify_consistent_recolor is never asked to adjudicate an opcode change it has no model for; a function may legitimately carry both stages. `ori rD,rS,0` is a real third copy form and is DELIBERATELY excluded: it is absent from the measured population, and the rule accepts only forms its tests exercise. THE GUARD FIRES ON REAL DATA, which is the evidence that it is not decorative: game/game/controls::MtapOpenPort is a member of this family by signature (ours `li r3,1` at +0xac, target `mr r3,r28`) and is REFUSED, because +0xac is the destination of the `bne` at +0x98 — r28 would have to hold 1 on both incoming edges, which a local scan cannot establish. That function stays source work or a park; do not route around the refusal.
